senses.gloss:
kaccha (Ep. Ind., Vol. XIV, p. 177), a field bordering on a stream; land near a well (Ep. Ind., Vol XXXIV, p. 175, line 15).
 (EI 22), a resolution.

kacchaka (EI 19), a low hill.
 (IA 18), wrongly read also as kasthaka; cf. khalaka-kacchaka-bhūmī-sahitā as an epithet of the gift land; probably, ‘land around a well’. See kūpaṃ khalakaṃ kacchakaṃ (Ind. Ant., Vol. XVIII, p. 114, text line 55, cf. line 43); also kūpa-kaccha (Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXIV, p. 175, text line 15).
kacchapa, cf. sa-matsya-kacchapa (IE 8-5); tortoise; see jala-kara.
